argument_summary: The current record does not support caveat-free certification, but it does support certification on a disclosed, qualified basis. The strongest admissible reading is that aggregate readiness is above threshold and there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, while the unresolved freight hazmat documentation weakness remains material enough that it should be disclosed in the certification/model-card record. On that reading, the defensible action is not to reject certification outright, but to treat it as caveated compliance tied to explicit disclosure of the limitation.
claims_about_business_cost: A caveated certification avoids treating the record as cleaner than it is while also avoiding unnecessary escalation beyond what the admissible evidence requires. The remaining uncertainty is narrow and already identified: the hazmat documentation slice and the incomplete mitigation details. That is more proportionately handled through disclosed limitation and monitoring than by treating the entire certification basis as unsupported.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not require zero residual risk. The admissible evidence supports a deployment decision that measures and manages residual risk, and public model-card guidance supports documenting limitations and evaluation results. At the same time, the stated policy text is clear that certification without material caveats requires either no current material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The draft runbook does not satisfy that higher bar. So the policy-compliant position is qualified certification with disclosure, not unqualified certification and not a claim that the draft mitigation alone closes the gap.
concessions: The current record does not support caveat-free certification.
The draft mitigation runbook is incomplete because owner and alert threshold are still TBD.
The model-card draft statement that there are no known material limitations is in tension with the unresolved hazmat issue.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance or a finalized approved mitigation that would remove the disclosure requirement.
